environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed on EKS cluster with Istio service mesh (v1.19). The function is wrapped in a Kubernetes pod (using AWS Lambda Web Adapter) in the 'notification-service' namespace. An Istio AuthorizationPolicy is applied at the namespace level with a DENY rule for requests originating from any source principal outside 'cluster.local/ns/api-gateway-ns/sa/apigw-service-account'. Additionally, a PeerAuthentication policy enforces STRICT mTLS for the namespace. The ingress path requires traversal through the 'api-gateway-ns' namespace envoy sidecar which has a RequestAuthentication policy validating JWT tokens issued by the internal OIDC provider (issuer: https://oidc.internal.example.com). External traffic hitting the mesh ingress gateway is routed through a VirtualService that only matches paths /v1/notifications/* with header 'x-request-source: internal-gateway'. The AuthorizationPolicy spec: {action: DENY, rules: [{from: [{source: {notNamespaces: ['api-gateway-ns']}}]}]}. Raw pod-to-pod communication from outside the mesh is blocked by NetworkPolicy restricting ingress to only port 8080 from pods with label 'istio-injection: enabled'.

config.runtime: python3.9 in K8s pod with Lambda Web Adapter
config.authorization_policy: DENY action for source not in api-gateway-ns namespace
config.request_authentication: JWT validation required at ingress, issuer https://oidc.internal.example.com
config.virtual_service: path match /v1/notifications/* with required header x-request-source: internal-gateway
config.network_policy: ingress only from pods with istio-injection=enabled on port 8080
